items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Eddie Condon brought Pee Wee Russell to Disneyland the year I didn't go. I never heard either one of them in person.

ctx.x: What was your parents’ musical tastes like?

They liked older popular music. I mean they were not jazz fans, record collectors, with a copy of Brian Rust to say, “Oh yeah that was recorded by Bix and Red Nichols.” They just, if it was good, and well played, they liked it. So when I got an interest in the older forms of ragtime and things like that, they were ready for that and they liked it because they’d grown up during the Swing Era, which was just an extension of that if you want to © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

think of it in a straight line. My dad was a pianist, just a hobby pianist, not a professional, but he had records of Jelly Roll Morton and Fats Waller and I heard those things, they didn’t get through to me until years later. But generally if I liked it, they’d like it. And they were real supportive of my goals and taking me to hear live jazz whenever possible. That was problem though. In California, you have to be 21 to get into a club, and they card like crazy. And you can’t sneak in and drink a Coke. So…
